transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-07-06 11:00 AM ET / 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Evelyn Ross (Arden CISO), Carlos Mendez (Arden Cloud Architect), Priya Shah (Arden Security Engineer)

[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everybody, thanks for joining. Quick intros? We'll run through Redwood Private architecture, focus on VPC/isolation, ingress and egress controls, and then open to questions.
[00:00:18] Evelyn: Hi, Evelyn here. CISO at Arden. We're looking for a private deployment option — no public internet ingress, tight egress, KMS with HSM and long audit log retention.
[00:00:28] Carlos: Carlos, cloud architect, I'll drive the network side.
[00:00:31] Priya: Priya, security eng. I'll review firewall rules and SIEM integration.
[00:00:36] Ravi: Thanks, all. I'll kick off with the high-level topology, then dive into specifics.

[00:01:05] Ravi: So there's two patterns we see: "private control plane" where the control plane sits in your VPC or we run a hybrid control plane — we also support an isolated, customer-managed control plane for on-prem installs. For VPC deployments, we typically create dedicated subnets, NAT instance or egress-only gateway, and a transit gateway peering for multi-region.
[00:01:40] Evelyn: Quick clarification — when you say control plane in our VPC, does that mean Redwood won't have any public-facing endpoints into our network? We need zero public ingress.
[00:01:50] Maya: Correct, you can choose a private control plane that talks to Redwood management over a private peering or a customer-managed control plane — in the latter, Redwood never initiates inbound connections; all agent communication is outbound from your side, or via a private link.
[00:02:10] Carlos: So likely we want agent outbound only. We have strict policy: no inbound port openings.

[00:02:32] Ravi: For agent model updates and metrics there are two options: 1) TLS over private link / VPC endpoint; 2) customer-hosted relay in their VPC that does egress to Redwood's backend over an approved transit. We prefer option 1 for lower ops friction.
[00:02:53] Priya: On TLS — we need mutual TLS or at least certificate pinning. How does Redwood authenticate agents?
[00:03:01] Maya: We support mTLS as part of the private deployment package; for VPC we can provision certs using your PKI or integrate with your Vault. We also support SAML SSO for user access to the console and granular RBAC.

[00:03:26] [00:03:30] Ravi: Let me share screen — (audio note: screen share described) here's the typical 3-node private cluster: control plane sits in a management subnet, then inference nodes in private subnets across AZs. We place a NAT for egress and a managed endpoint for peering to your transit GW.
[00:03:58] Carlos: Can you show where the firewall sits? We're using Palo Alto as our perimeter and expect microsegmentation too.
[00:04:06] Ravi: Sure — firewall sits at the VPC edge and we recommend security group per role: control plane SG, inference node SG, and bastion SG. On top of that use NACLs for subnet-level rules. For customers using Palo Alto we often terminate Transit GW into their hub VPC where the firewall does ingress/egress filtering.

[00:04:40] Evelyn: Egress policy is big for us. We need to restrict egress to a small set of Redwood endpoints and also have all egress proxied through our egress firewall. Can Redwood work with that?
[00:04:50] Maya: Yes. Typical pattern: you restrict outbound to specific IP ranges and DNS names; Redwood provides a published egress CIDR list for the private deployment. We also support configuring the agents to use your corporate outbound proxy so you can inspect traffic.
[00:05:14] Priya: Do you publish an egress IP list or do you recommend a PrivateLink? IP lists get messy.
[00:05:20] Ravi: We provide a CIDR and also recommend PrivateLink / VPC Endpoint to avoid public egress. If you must egress to public, we can pin to maintaining stable IP ranges; for on-prem, we prefer a customer-hosted relay.

[00:05:50] [00:06:05] Carlos: About network isolation — do your inference nodes require outbound access for model downloads at startup? We want to vet the data plane flows.
[00:06:12] Ravi: Good question. Models can be pre-staged in your storage (S3 or on-prem NFS) to avoid outbound download. If using Redwood-hosted model store, the inference nodes will need outbound TLS to fetch model artifacts — again we can route that through PrivateLink or the customer relay.
[00:06:35] Evelyn: We will insist on pre-staging models into our S3 behind our VPC endpoints. No outbound artifact retrieval from public.

[00:06:50] Maya: Noted. On encryption — data at rest is encrypted using customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS integration; for on-prem we support HSM-backed keys (YubiHSM/Thales) or integration with HashiVault.
[00:07:05] Priya: We use an HSM provider and need attestation that the key material never leaves HSM. Does Redwood support HSM-backed KMS where keys are never exported?
[00:07:13] Ravi: Yes, we can integrate with your HSM/KMS — the service uses envelope encryption and the CMK is never exported. For private deployments the KMS calls are done within your network; if you use Redwood-managed KMS we can support HSM-backed key stores as an enterprise option.

[00:07:40] [00:08:00] Evelyn: Audit logs — retention is 7 years for us. What are your defaults and can we ship logs to our SIEM?
[00:08:07] Maya: Default retention on hosted is 90 days, but for private we can configure longer retention and ship logs to your SIEM via syslog, S3 bucket, or direct API integration. We support activity logs, admin actions, model changes, and inference metadata — note inference payload logging is opt-in.
[00:08:35] Priya: We need immutable logs and tamper-evidence. Is there an append-only option?
[00:08:42] Ravi: We can stream logs to an append-only S3 bucket with bucket-lock enabled, or to your SIEM with write-only ingestion endpoints. We also support signed audit records for admin actions.

[00:09:10] Carlos: For network segmentation, can we put inference nodes in isolated subnets with no route to the public internet and only allow egress to internal S3 endpoints?
[00:09:19] Ravi: Absolutely — inference nodes can be in private subnets without internet routing; model fetches from private S3 VPC endpoint, metrics/health telemetry over PrivateLink, and all management traffic via peering.

[00:09:48] [00:10:05] Evelyn: What about RBAC and SSO? We need SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC so product teams can only access specific models or routes.
[00:10:15] Maya: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. RBAC can be scoped by project, model, and environment. For private deployments RBAC enforcement is local to the control plane and syncs with your IdP.
[00:10:36] Priya: Will the audit logs include admin role changes and SCIM events?
[00:10:41] Ravi: Yes; SCIM provisioning, role changes, console logins, and API key events are logged.

[00:11:05] Maya: Quick pause — are there any blockers so far?
[00:11:09] Evelyn: Main blockers: inbound restriction (solved), long-term audit retention (needs contract), and KMS/HSM proof. Also need to validate egress flows to make sure we can inspect and log them.

[00:11:30] [00:12:00] Ravi: Let's talk firewalling details. We have two recommended modes: hub-and-spoke with Transit GW where firewall in the hub enforces egress and ingress, or sidecar firewalls per VPC for microsegmentation. For high security customers we typically do hub firewall + microsegmentation.
[00:12:22] Carlos: We prefer hub & spoke with Palo Alto VM-Series in hub. How does Redwood integrate with Transit Gateway route tables?
[00:12:29] Ravi: Redwood's deployer will set up route tables so the management subnet routes to your Transit GW attachments. We provide the attachment configuration and you own the hub firewall policies. Redwood doesn't manage your firewall rules.

[00:12:55] Priya: IDS/IPS and egress monitoring — can we mirror traffic from inference nodes to our IDS?
[00:13:01] Ravi: Yes, traffic mirroring to your IDS/monitoring VPC is supported. For higher security, we place inference nodes in dedicated subnets and enable VPC Traffic Mirroring to your analysis appliances. There may be perf costs but customers accept that for compliance.

[00:13:32] [00:13:40] Evelyn: Data residency — all data must stay in-region. If we deploy in our us-east-1 VPC, can Redwood guarantee no cross-region replication?
[00:13:46] Maya: For private VPC deployments, data residency is enforced: the storage, model artifacts, and logs remain in your region and under your account if you choose customer-managed storage. Redwood-managed artifacts can be pinned to region but we'd document the replication policy — for Arden we recommend customer-managed S3 to be explicit.

[00:14:10] Carlos: For HA, what's the recommended node topology across AZs? We need failover within region, not cross-region.
[00:14:18] Ravi: Recommended: 3 inference nodes across 3 AZs with the control plane nodes in 2 AZs and a quorum. For persistence, use replicated block storage on your side or EBS with multi-AZ replication. We'll provide topology diagrams and expected RTO/RPO.

[00:14:45] [00:15:00] Priya: How are secrets handled on nodes? We don't want plain text API keys on disk.
[00:15:06] Ravi: Secrets are pulled from your Vault at boot over mTLS and cached in memory; we avoid storing plaintext secrets on disk. For on-prem we can integrate with HashiVault or your KMS provider.

[00:15:34] Maya: Let's cover SIEM integration — what format do you need?
[00:15:38] Priya: We prefer JSON over syslog to our SIEM ingest endpoint; for large volumes S3 dump with Glue is OK.
[00:15:46] Ravi: We stream audit and operational logs in JSON; inference telemetry can be sent separately and is opt-in. We can provide a CloudWatch or Azure Monitor mapping if needed.

[00:16:10] [00:16:30] Carlos: About firewall rule examples — can you provide a sample set for supporting the private deployment?
[00:16:36] Maya: Yes, we'll send a sample Terraform and security group/NACL examples. That will include ports for mTLS agent outbound, health check ports, and model fetch endpoints.

[00:16:58] Priya: For the egress CIDR list, how often does that change?
[00:17:04] Ravi: In stable deployments we aim to keep ranges stable; however maintenance windows or scale events could add ephemeral ranges. For critical customers we recommend PrivateLink to avoid whitelisting churn.

[00:17:30] [00:18:00] Evelyn: What about penetration testing and compliance evidence? We need SOC 2 Type II report, ISO evidence, and your latest pentest summary.
[00:18:09] Maya: We'll share SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certificates under NDA; we also have a pentest summary and can coordinate scoping for your security team.

[00:18:35] Ravi: One more network note — for on-prem deployments behind strict egress, we provide an offline install bundle and offline updates. Customers can run full inference without outbound if models are pre-staged.

[00:18:58] Carlos: That helps. For monitoring, do you require outbound metrics, or can those be pushed to our Prometheus endpoint?
[00:19:06] Ravi: We support push and pull models: metrics exporters for Prometheus that run in your VPC and push to your Prometheus/Grafana. If you want Redwood observability, that can be configured via PrivateLink.

[00:19:30] [00:19:45] Priya: Do you provide signed attestations for the deployed binaries or images? We require image signing verification.
[00:19:52] Maya: Yes, we publish signed container image digests and support attestation checks at deploy time. For on-prem we can provide SBOM and signed manifests.

[00:20:20] Ravi: Wrapping up technical items — I'll enumerate what we'll send: network diagram, terraform examples, CIDR list (or PrivateLink config), HA topology and throughput estimates, and sample firewall rules.

[00:20:40] Evelyn: Thanks. Contractual items — can we get an SLA for private deployments and retention in the contract?
[00:20:47] Maya: Yes, SLA and retention can be negotiated in the enterprise contract; we'll loop legal after we confirm technical fit.

[00:21:10] [00:21:25] Carlos: One more question on logging — are inference payloads redacted by default? We don't want PII stored unless we opt into it.
[00:21:33] Ravi: Inference payload logging is disabled by default; you can opt-in and configure redaction. We provide client-side redaction hooks as well.

[00:21:55] Priya: For encryption in transit, aside from mTLS, do you support explicit cipher suites and FIPS modes?
[00:22:04] Ravi: We can enable FIPS-compliant cipher suites and support FIPS mode for our on-prem packages. Cipher lists can be configured to meet your compliance posture.

[00:22:30] [00:22:48] Evelyn: Ok — sounds promising. Next steps and timeline? We're aiming to start a POC mid-July.
[00:22:55] Maya: We'll target week of 2026-07-20 for the POC. I'll send the diagrams and artifacts by 2026-07-08. Ravi will send topology and throughput by 2026-07-13.

[00:23:20] Carlos: I'll coordinate firewall and Transit GW attachments with our network team and share a contact.

[00:23:25] Priya: I'll validate the log ingest and HSM requirements and get back with questions.

[00:23:40] Maya: Great, let's do a quick recap.
[00:23:43] Maya: Recap: Arden requires private deployment in-region, no public ingress, egress through inspected paths or PrivateLink, KMS/HSM integration with keys not exported, long-term audit retention, SIEM integration, SAML/SCIM + RBAC, and sample firewall rules. Redwood will provide network diagrams, Terraform samples, CIDR/PrivateLink configs, HA throughput estimates, SOC 2/ISO artifacts under NDA, and schedule POC for week of July 20.
[00:24:20] Evelyn: That matches our notes. Thanks.
[00:24:25] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with the artifacts and calendar invite for the POC.
[00:24:32] Carlos: Thanks, bye.
[00:24:34] Priya: Thanks, bye.
